- **Dalton Risner** — Risner said he has settled into a structured offseason routine after signing a new deal with Cincinnati and entering his eighth NFL season. He framed the work as part of getting his body ready for the “17-plus game grind,” but the item does not specify his exact role or lineup competition. [2]

- **Zac Taylor** — Taylor said he is “really excited” about the group the Bengals assembled this offseason, pointing to the way the roster was built through free agency, releases, trades, and the draft. The broader takeaway is that Cincinnati is leaning hard into trench upgrades, which raises the stakes for coaching if the roster stays healthy. [5, 3]

- **Swayze Bozeman** — The Bengals claimed Bozeman off waivers and used the move to fill a 90-man roster spot, making him their first veteran linebacker addition of the offseason. That matters because Cincinnati had tried to add at linebacker earlier and now has another body in a room that needed help. [4]

- **Isaiah Nwokobia** — Cincinnati signed Nwokobia as an undrafted free agent safety to reach the 90-man roster limit. The move adds another depth piece in the secondary, though the item does not specify a path to playing time. [4]

- **Cashius Howell** — The Bengals have not yet signed Howell, one of the two unsigned players from their rookie class ahead of minicamp. His status is notable because he is one of the top two selections still out of the fold, so his eventual signing will be worth watching for roster timing. [5]

- **Tacario Davis** — Davis also remains unsigned even after most of the rookie class was finalized before minicamp. That leaves one third-round pick still not officially in the fold, making his contract status the cleanest remaining rookie question. [5]

- **Ted Karras** — Karras said the addition of Connor Lew and Brian Parker II at center does not change his mindset, stressing that veterans have to “fight” for their jobs. He even called both rookies after the draft, which suggests Cincinnati’s interior-line competition is being handled directly rather than quietly. [6]
